avatars.program:
Keep every rep and hold crisp. Planche stays on parallettes to respect the wrist, and all skill sets stop before shape breaks. Weighted Dip uses two tracks each week: one specific +60 kg volume exposure and one heavier strength-reserve exposure to make +60 kg feel easier.

Weeks 2-4: build by small rep or set additions first, then small load bumps where noted. If BJJ fatigue runs high, keep the listed load but stop 1 rep earlier on the final set rather than grinding.

Pain/substitutions: if wrists feel irritated, shorten planche holds by 1-2 seconds and keep perfect protraction on parallettes; do not switch to floor planche work. If elbows or shoulders feel beat up on dips, use the same load with slightly lower reps and longer rest. If front rack or knees are irritated, Front Squat can become Paused Front Squat at 5-10 kg less for the same reps.

avatars.program:
Keep the main lifts crisp and low-fatigue around MMA. Weighted Chin-up stays the anchor, Human Flag gets two fresh direct exposures, and lower body work is enough to keep strength and pop without stealing from sport.

Weeks 2-4: add small load jumps on Weighted Chin-up, extend One-Leg Tuck Human Flag holds by 1-2 seconds where quality stays high, and keep lower-body volume steady. Week 4 consolidates with a slightly heavier chin-up top exposure, not an all-out test.

If the medial elbow gets hot, first cut 1 back-off set from Weighted Chin-up or reduce the curl dose, keep heavy top work clean, and use straps on Romanian Deadlift if grip irritation is feeding the elbow. For Human Flag, stop each set as soon as the line or shoulder position degrades; if needed, shorten the hold rather than forcing sloppy reps.
